interface.title: Dunceious v3.7.3 ("Because geniality is overpriced")
interface.field: Molecular biology / comparative genomics (viral and phage genome annotation and alignment viewing)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploration and curation: inspecting annotated genomes, comparing aligned variants, curating and exporting feature sets
interface.what_it_is_for: A browser-only GenBank/FASTA viewer where you load genomes, overlay a multiple alignment with a conservation track, zoom from overview to bases and codon translations, search motifs, turn selections or hits into annotations, and export sequences/annotations/projects.

data.note: First session: phage-t7-NC_001604.gb, phage-t3-NC_003298.gb, phage-13a-NC_011045.gb. The repo ships two files named aligned.fasta: examples/nucleotide/t7-phages/aligned.fasta, which holds the T7 IDs (NC_001604, NC_011045, NC_003298), and the SARS-CoV-2 one (NC_045512, OL461693, OR279985, OR323867). The test-file copy put both under the same name, so the SARS-CoV-2 copy overwrote the T7 one. Uploading it onto the phages therefore produced the app's 'Sequence mismatch' ID check; this was a test-setup collision, not a fault of the app or the repo. After removing the phages, I loaded sars-cov-2-NC_045512.gb plus variants.gb (3 records), then aligned.fasta, which applied successfully (29,903 columns). human-insulin-NP_000198.gb was used only to test the one-molecule-type rule.

tree.general: Load related genomes, inspect their annotations down to single bases and codons, compare aligned variants, find motifs, and save a curated feature set
tree.specific: Use Dunceious to view T7-family phage and SARS-CoV-2 variant GenBank records, read the T7 gene 10 frameshift at base zoom and SARS-CoV-2 spike mutations in alignment view, search with IUPAC and fuzzy matching, and export GFF3/FASTA/project JSON

features.name: Semantic-zoom sequence viewport with range selection
features.general: A genome map that changes how much it shows as you zoom: feature arrows and mismatch density far out, then individual bases and translated codons close in. Dragging marks a range, which you can then zoom to, centre or clear.
features.specific: Visual Viewport: overview minimap + Go to… box + Fit/+/−; in Select mode drag across a sequence row to make a selection, then Zoom Sel shows bases with Translation rows (including −1 frameshift frames); Pan mode drags the view.
steps: Type a position in Go to… and press Enter (or press Fit)
Drag across a sequence row in Select mode to mark a range
Press Zoom Sel to fill the view with the range
Read bases and the amino-acid rows; hover feature badges for details
Switch to Pan mode and drag to move along
serves_tasks: Zoom to single bases and codons at a site of interest
Zoom into a divergent region to read deletions and point mutations

features.name: Selection inspector with per-record coordinate mapping
features.general: A side panel for the current range: it shows the range in shared alignment columns and each record's own coordinates, lets you edit start/end, and exports it or makes it a feature.
features.specific: Selection Inspector: Range/Length, editable Start/End, 'Original coordinates' per record (e.g. alignment 21,757–21,776 = OL461693 21,686–21,699), and FASTA / JSON / + Annot buttons.
steps: Make a selection in the viewport
Read or edit Start/End and the per-record original coordinates
Press FASTA to download the slice from every record
Or press + Annot to open Create Feature prefilled with the range
serves_tasks: Turn a selected range into a named annotation
Export the selected range from every record

features.name: Create/edit feature dialog
features.general: A form for one feature: name, type, strand, colour, start/end or several joined segments, and free-form key/value qualifiers. It is used both for new features and for editing existing ones.
features.specific: Create Feature / Metadata Inspector: Target Sequence, Display Name, Feature Key (gene, CDS, regulatory, primer…), Strand, colour, Start/End or Segments with + Add segment, regenerated GenBank location, Qualifiers with + Add qualifier.
steps: Open it from + Annot, a search hit's Annotate, or a row's pencil
Set name, key and strand
Adjust coordinates or segments
Add qualifiers (optionally search details)
Press Create/Apply; the feature appears in the viewport and hub
serves_tasks: Turn a selected range into a named annotation
Promote a search hit to an annotation
Open and read one feature's full record

features.name: Motif search with IUPAC and fuzzy modes, hit cards and annotate
features.general: Search every loaded sequence for a short pattern, either exactly with ambiguity codes or allowing a set share of edits. Each hit becomes a card with identity and strand, and you can jump to it or keep it as a feature.
features.specific: Sequence Search: IUPAC | Fuzzy (Whole query | Local, Min query identity slider), Strand (Both/Forward/Reverse), Result limit; results grouped per record with Select all / Join all, hit cards showing % identity and edits, query/hit alignment in the viewport, and Annotate.
steps: Choose IUPAC or Fuzzy (and Whole query or Local)
Set strand, result limit and minimum identity
Type the query and press Enter
Click a hit card to jump; mismatches are highlighted against a Query row
Press Annotate to save the hit as a feature
serves_tasks: Search with a degenerate (ambiguity-code) pattern
Search allowing mismatches
Promote a search hit to an annotation

features.name: Imported alignment overlay with conservation track
features.general: Lay a multiple alignment computed elsewhere over the loaded records. Records are matched by ID and gaps inserted, features shift into alignment columns, and a conservation profile under the rows shows where sequences diverge.
features.specific: Upload pre-aligned FASTA (IDs must match active records; otherwise the log reports 'Sequence mismatch' and lists missing/extra IDs), then the Conservation layer toggle draws a conservation track that dips at variable columns. Per-variant difference marks come from Compare (f6), not from this layer.
steps: Load the records
Upload the pre-aligned FASTA
Check the log for 'External alignment applied' or a mismatch error
Turn on Conservation and press Fit
Zoom on dips to read the columns
serves_tasks: Overlay a multiple alignment produced elsewhere
Read where aligned sequences diverge along the genome

features.name: Compare-to-reference highlighting
features.general: Pick one aligned sequence as the reference and recolour the others to show only differences or only identities. Matching residues can be drawn as dots, and gaps and ambiguity codes are handled explicitly.
features.specific: Compare popover: Highlight Off / Differences / Identity, Reference dropdown (any record), 'Show identical residues as dots'; the reference row gets a REF badge and the button reads 'vs <ID>'. At Fit it draws per-variant difference ticks along each row.
steps: Press Compare
Choose Differences or Identity
Pick the reference record
Toggle dots for identical residues
Zoom to read individual substitutions and gaps
serves_tasks: Highlight differences from a chosen reference
Read where aligned sequences diverge along the genome
Zoom into a divergent region to read deletions and point mutations

features.name: Annotation hub table with jump-to-viewport
features.general: A searchable, filterable table of every feature in every record, with a mini-map per record. Each row has info/edit/locate/delete actions, and locate opens the map at that feature with a 'back to table' chip.
features.specific: Annotation Hub > By sequence: Search annotations (/), type chips (CDS, gene, regulatory…), strand filter (All/→/←), Compact/Comfortable, per-record mini-map; row icons info/edit/locate/delete; locate → Visual Viewport with 'Back to Annotation Hub' chip.
steps: Type a term in Search annotations or click a type chip
Hover a row to see its tooltip and icons
Press locate to jump to the feature in the viewport
Use 'Back to Annotation Hub' to return to the highlighted row
serves_tasks: Find a feature by text search in the annotation table
Jump from a table row to that feature in the map view
Filter the feature table by type

features.name: Cross-genome feature presence matrix
features.general: Group features with the same name across all genomes, show which genomes have each one, and flag missing, duplicated or unusual-length copies with a one-click filter for just the abnormal ones.
features.specific: Annotation Hub > By feature: per-gene cards ('in 4 of 4 sequences', median position, length range), presence/duplicate/odd-length squares, organism-grouped sidebar list, and 'Only missing or odd length' toggle (surfaces OL461693's truncated ORF8).
steps: Open the By feature tab
Optionally limit by type chip
Read presence squares and per-genome coordinates
Press 'Only missing or odd length' to keep anomalies
serves_tasks: Line up the same gene across all genomes and flag the abnormal ones

features.name: Export wizard (sequence picker + format + preview)
features.general: A two-step export: choose which records by quick sets or checkboxes, then a format. Format-specific options appear, and a summary says exactly what the file will hold before you download it.
features.specific: Export sequences: quick sets All / Selected in hub / Matching filters / Shown in hub / Shown in viewport / None + checkboxes; formats FASTA, GenBank, GFF3, Dunceious project; options such as Keep alignment gaps, NCBI header, annotation types, only hub-filtered annotations; 'What this file will contain' preview and file name.
steps: Press Export
Choose records (quick set or checkboxes)
Choose a format
Set options (e.g. Keep alignment gaps)
Check the preview and press Export
serves_tasks: Export one genome's annotations for a genome browser
Export aligned sequences with the alignment-gaps option

features.name: Batch ingestion with ID de-duplication and session-type guard
features.general: Load many sequence files at once. Multi-record files split into separate records, a repeated ID is renamed instead of overwritten, and loading a different molecule type is blocked with an explanation.
features.specific: Drop input batch / + Add sequences…: variants.gb → 3 records; re-uploading NC_045512 adds NC_045512_1; a peptide .gb in a nucleotide session shows 'Session type mismatch — clear all records first'; records can be removed one at a time from Record Navigator. Every step is written to the Log Terminal.
steps: Pick or drop GenBank/FASTA files
Read the Log Terminal for records added
Check renamed IDs in Record Navigator
Dismiss the mismatch dialog if a wrong-type file was added
